term: endpoint-sound contingent predecessor of a necessary potential causer
definition: ContingentPredecessorControl fixes the existing ContingentOnly PSR ontology and replaces only ordinary Causes with w=false ∧ source≠target. Both candidates exist at false and cause each other there; at true only candidate false exists and there are no causal edges. Candidate false is necessary and has the full OtherDirectedPotentialCause role. All edges have distinct existing endpoints. The necessary-only union is empty and well-founded because true is contingent; nevertheless true exists at false and actually causes false there. The conjunction explicitly negates the no-contingent-predecessor bridge and named underivedness while retaining the other four backgrounds of the named theorem. It does not satisfy or assert worldwise causal well-foundedness: false has a two-cycle. It is outside the owner's acyclic-world setting and tests only the weaker backgrounds without pointwise causal WF.
note: A single finite formal omission interpretation, not a possible temporal history or metaphysical counterexample. The cause-as-support choice is explicit; endpoint presence is not a loophole. This tests the exact theorem's bridge, not every stronger causal theory.
